upstream.required_input: accepted M1 canonical version and source-linked statements

track_2_relevance: LangGraph orchestrates the durable multi-step M1-to-M2 workflow.
A localhost vLLM model proposes semantic CUE, CHANGE and SURPRISE roles through a strict structured-output contract.
The local Agent keeps private source content outside graph checkpoints and traces.
SQLite remains canonical truth while the LangGraph SQLite checkpointer stores only the orchestration cursor.
Trusted user confirmation, not model output, decides whether a proposed moment is critical.

workflow.resume_cursor: LangGraph AsyncSqliteSaver sharing the application database
workflow.compile_policy: one graph instance compiled at application startup

invariants: Every map binds to one explicit base_m1_version_id.
Every moment references source statements declared by the map.
Semantic role proposals must reference every eligible current statement exactly once and may not reference any unknown statement.
Model unavailability, timeout or invalid structured output stops safely without a regex or keyword fallback.
Agent output may only propose criticality; USER_CONFIRMED and UNRESOLVED are explicit trusted user transitions.
The map cannot be confirmed while any moment remains AGENT_PROPOSED.
Missing time remains MISSING with an unresolved reason and no invented label.
Conflicting time remains CONFLICTING and references both conflicting statements.
A correction invalidates M2 only when it changes a declared dependency statement.
An invalidated artifact remains visible but is not presented as current.
